summary: Packet C final review of review_artifacts/runtime_self_test_invocation_code_design.md at full-source SHA-256 629f2159a420470a8e96977ce70904b74743f21ecc405f75fa9d896911926cf6. The two shard reports were treated as evidence only and re-checked line by line against this exact candidate; neither shard's verdict was inherited. The authority shard reports a different candidate hash (b7893a64...), and the code-truth shard's single low finding quotes line 201 as 'required_tests: [claude_boundary_preflight, codex_boundary_preflight, provider_not_called_negative, existing_transport_regression]', whereas line 201 of this exact candidate reads 'required_tests: [claude_boundary_preflight, codex_boundary_preflight, self_test_boundary_admits_provider_transport, provider_not_called_negative, existing_transport_regression]' — the live positive control now has exactly one module owner, so that finding does not apply here. Re-verified independently: the ten primary-flow edges (66-75) each carry exactly one interface_id or error_code and each resolves to one contract row (77-116, 118-159); every interface states exact input, successful output, effects and error codes; every error row states owner, condition, meaning and caller action; interface and error identities are unique, each declares a semantic owner and is marked declared or referenced; the three slices' required_tests are exact unions of their modules' required_tests (168+190=236; 179+201+212=244; 223=251) with 27 distinct tests each owned by one module and appearing in one slice; every excluded surface has exactly one later owning slice_id and completion gate, and each deferred surface is included in the slice named (233-235, 240, 243, 248); hash domains are named and tested for the request identity codec (256, 309-312), intent_sha256 (259, 318-320) and operation_payload_sha256 (260, 320-322); claimed field absences are fenced by full dataclass field-set comparison rather than a denylist (279, 312); and behavioral guards are paired with live positive controls (314-316, 322, 326-327). The two modules absent from all slices are exactly the two with disposition: retain (215, 226), and their tests are still assigned to slices. All eighteen requirements are satisfied and no findings are raised. This is external content review only: it is not implementation approval, registered Runtime review, exact-commit Engineering Review, release admission, or permission, and nothing was edited or approved.

requirements.requirement: there is no hidden fallback, parallel authority, or ad hoc bypass; and
requirements.evidence: Fallback is refused in the error semantics and the module rules: 152 'changed closure requires a new execution and never falls back between boundary kinds', 124 'never infer self-test, fabricate begin/boundary evidence or change provider', 199 prohibits implicit_provider_fallback and production_authority_minting, 267 'Provider/model selection and fallback do not change.' Parallel authority is refused explicitly at 264 ('no second logical interface or permission authority is introduced') and structurally: the new callback returns None and no peer record (98-99), boundary admission remains the referenced T2 09 owner's (217), and the two boundary groups are 'complete, mutually exclusive, independently resolvable and structurally fenced' (274). Ad hoc bypass is closed at 265 (neither-evidence is rejected before provider), 325 (a self-test host missing the callback fails before provider entry), 314-315 (callback bypass rejected before the provider counter changes) and 285 (no publication, Ledger destination, record deletion or pointer promotion).

prose_review: The document reads as a governing artifact rather than a narrative. The intended result is stated once (30-33) and every later section either constrains it or proves it; the reader can move from the flow, to the contracts, to the modules, to the slices without re-deriving anything, and the Chinese opening paragraph (3-5) sets scope and exclusions before any mechanism appears. The strongest prose is where the basis refuses to let a claim rest on wording: line 260's 'payload_hash_binding proves byte-identical recomputation and a one-field mutation failure, never equality of stored hashes alone' and line 312's 'field-set assertions compare the full dataclass field set, not a denylist' both convert an assertion into a control that can fail, and line 333's 'a test double cannot establish transport support' correctly refuses to let deterministic evidence stand in for real-provider evidence. Ownership language is disciplined throughout: referenced identities are described in the peer's terms (98, 100, 152, 217) instead of being restated in this basis's voice, and line 264 draws the one distinction that keeps the design honest, separating a second physical binding from a second authority. Meaning is preserved against the bound Designs where the excerpts allow checking: staging versus authoritative output (83, 115) tracks T2 08 §11 and §12; the receipt-before-effect rule (107) tracks T2 08 §12's authorize_operation row; the operation-free in-process exception (265, 274) tracks the third row of T2 08 §5.2; and the fail-closed, no-substitution stance of T2 09 §5-§6 is carried into 124 and 152 without softening. Three prose-level improvements are worth making before the basis is frozen, none of which changes a contract: line 268 names three of result_normalization's four required regressions and silently omits result_schema_regression, which is correctly present in both the module list (212) and the slice list (244), so the sentence understates its own assignment; line 276's 'neither is rejected before a provider call' parses awkwardly and would be clearer as 'a request with neither is rejected before any provider call'; and the frozen-hash table (299-307) would better match line 214 if it either added rows for invocation_failure_recording.py and invocation_result_assembly.py or stated that it freezes only the sources this basis may modify. The self-check (342-350) is appropriately demoted to author observation and does not attempt to stand in for this review.
